title: Anisotropic Superconductivity with Enhanced Critical Field in Strained RuO2
authors: Younes Ghorbani, Samuel Poage, Xuehsi Gao, Luka Mitrovic, Neha Wadehra, Benjamin Gregory, Suchismita Sarker, Betul Pamuk, Andrej Singer, Darrell G. Schlom, Chun Ning Lau, Kaveh Ahadi
abstract: The superconductivity in RuO2 emerges under strain. RuO2 is also an altermagnet candidate. The nature of superconductivity and its relation with neighboring orders, however, are not understood. To address this problem, we grew epitaxial RuO2 films on TiO2(100) and TiO2(110) single crystal substrates and studied the electronic transport and emergent superconductivity along various crystallographic directions. We show that the superconducting transition strongly depends on the growth orientation and the crystallographic direction of the transport in the RuO2 films. We also observe a strong violation of Pauli paramagnetic limit with in-plane applied magnetic field which we attribute to strong spin-orbit scattering. These results offer opportunities for epitaxially engineered superconductors.
summary: This work reports on the discovery of anisotropic superconductivity in strained $	ext{RuO}_2$ thin films grown epitaxially. By measuring transport properties along different crystallographic directions and applying magnetic fields, the authors demonstrate that strain significantly enhances the critical field beyond theoretical limits. The findings highlight the crucial role of spin-orbit coupling and epitaxial strain in engineering high-performance superconducting materials.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the nature of superconductivity in $	ext{RuO}_2$ and how its properties are governed by epitaxial strain and crystallographic direction.
main_result: Superconductivity is strongly anisotropic, exhibiting enhanced critical fields ($H_{c2,\parallel}$) that violate the Pauli paramagnetic limit, which is attributed to strong spin-orbit scattering effects in strained films.
method: The research combines experimental transport measurements (measuring sheet resistance vs. magnetic field along various directions) with theoretical modeling (DFT calculations and weak coupling theory).
model_or_system: The physical system is epitaxial $	ext{RuO}_2$ thin films grown on different single crystal substrates ($	ext{TiO}_2(100)$ and $	ext{TiO}_2(110)$), allowing for controlled strain engineering.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), critical magnetic fields ($H_{c2,\parallel}$ vs $H_{c2,\perp}$), critical current asymmetry, and the ratio of measured field to the Pauli limit ($H_{c2}/H_P$).
important_parameters: Epitaxial strain, spin-orbit scattering strength, dimensionality (suggesting 2D superconductivity), and temperature/magnetic field ranges.
main_assumptions: The analysis initially relies on weak coupling assumptions, but the strong enhancement suggests mechanisms beyond simple BCS theory are at play.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of superconducting transitions and critical fields on transport direction and applied in-plane magnetic field. XRD data confirms anisotropic strain relaxation defects.
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates how substrate choice dictates superconductivity, measures anisotropy via directional transport measurements, quantifies the violation of fundamental limits (Pauli), and theoretically models the enhancement mechanism using DFT and Ginzburg-Landau approaches.
why_interesting: While focused on unconventional superconductivity, the strong dependence on crystal orientation and strain provides a model for engineering superconducting properties in low-dimensional systems, which is relevant to quantum materials research.
